title_en: Regulations for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests

articles.content_en:
Article 9 A business operator shall provide consumers with relevant information on commodities or services in a true, comprehensive, and easy-to-understand manner, and shall not engage in false or misleading publicity to deceive or mislead consumers by means such as fabricating the operator's qualifications, credentials, or honors, fabricating transaction information of commodities or services or business data, or tampering with, fabricating, or concealing user reviews.
A business operator shall not set different prices or charging standards for the same commodity or service under the same transaction conditions without the consumer's knowledge.

Article 10 A business operator shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, clearly mark, in a conspicuous manner, information such as the name, price, and unit of measurement of the commodity or the items, content, price, and pricing method of the service, ensuring that the price tags and price lists are complete, the content is true and accurate, and the markings are clear and prominent.
Where a business operator provides services by means of automatic renewal or automatic extension, etc., it shall draw the consumer's attention in a conspicuous manner before the consumer accepts the service and before the date of automatic renewal or automatic extension.

Article 11 Consumers shall have the right to freely choose commodities or services. A business operator shall not, by means of violence, coercion, restriction of personal freedom, or by using technical means, compel or constructively compel consumers to purchase commodities or accept services, or exclude or restrict consumers from choosing commodities or services provided by other business operators. Where a business operator provides commodities or services through bundling, combination, or other means, it shall draw the consumer's attention in a conspicuous manner.

Article 12 Where a business operator, by means of commercial promotion, product recommendation, physical display, or notices, statements, or in-store announcements, provides commodities or services and makes commitments regarding the quantity, quality, price, after-sales service, liability bearing, etc., of the commodities or services, it shall fulfill such commitments to the consumers who purchase the commodities or accept the services.

Article 13 A business operator shall mark its true name and mark in a conspicuous position at its business premises.
Where a business operator provides commodities or services through the internet, television, telephone, mail order, or other means, it shall clearly mark or explain its true name and mark in a conspicuous manner on its homepage, video screen, voice, product catalogue, etc. Where commodities or services are actually provided by another business operator, it shall also provide consumers with information such as the name, business address, and contact information of that operator.
Where a business operator leases another person's counter or premises to provide commodities or services, or provides commodities or services through lectures, raffles, centralized experience, or other means, it shall mark its true name and mark in a conspicuous manner. The lessor of the counter or premises shall establish an in-store business management system, verify, update, and publicize the relevant information of the business operator for consumers to inquire.

Article 14 Where a business operator provides commodities or services through live streaming or other means, it shall perform the relevant obligations for the protection of consumers' rights and interests according to law.
The operator of the live streaming marketing platform shall establish and improve the consumer rights and interests protection system and specify the mechanism for resolving consumer disputes. In the event of a consumer dispute, the operator of the live streaming marketing platform shall, at the request of the consumer, provide relevant information about the operator of the live streaming room and the live streaming marketing personnel, as well as necessary information such as records of relevant business activities.
Where the content of a live stream released by the operator of the live streaming room or the live streaming marketing personnel constitutes a commercial advertisement, it shall perform the obligations of an advertisement publisher, advertisement operator, or advertisement endorser in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 15 A business operator shall not, through false or misleading publicity, fabricate or exaggerate the therapeutic, health care, or health preservation effects of commodities or services, thereby inducing elderly and other consumers to purchase commodities or services that obviously do not meet their actual needs.

Article 16 Where a business operator provides online game services, it shall comply with the national regulations and standards on the relevant time periods, duration, functions, and content of online game services, set up corresponding time management, permission management, consumption management, and other functions for minors, strictly conduct user verification at registration, login, and other stages, and protect the physical and mental health of minors according to law.

Article 17 Where a business operator uses standard terms, it shall comply with the provisions of Article 26 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests. A business operator shall not use standard terms to unreasonably exempt or mitigate its own liability, increase the consumer's liability, or restrict the consumer's rights, including the right to modify or dissolve a contract according to law, to choose litigation or arbitration for resolving consumer disputes, or to choose commodities or services of other business operators.

Article 18 The validity period for which a business operator agrees with a consumer to bear obligations such as return, replacement, or repair shall not be less than the requirements of the relevant provisions of the State. The validity period shall be calculated from the date on which the operator delivers the commodity to the consumer or completes the service; for commodities that need to be installed separately by the operator, the validity period shall be calculated from the date on which the commodity installation is completed. After the operator performs the replacement obligation for the consumer, the validity period for bearing obligations such as replacement and repair shall be recalculated from the date on which the replacement is completed. The time spent by the operator on repair shall not be counted in the above validity period.
Where a business operator performs the return obligation in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State or the agreement with the consumer, it shall refund the relevant amount in a lump sum according to the price shown on the invoice or other purchase vouchers or service receipts. If the operator can prove that the price actually paid by the consumer is inconsistent with the price shown on the invoice or other purchase vouchers or service receipts, the relevant amount shall be refunded according to the price actually paid by the consumer.

Article 19 Where a business operator sells commodities through the internet, television, telephone, mail order, or other means, it shall comply with the provisions of Article 25 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, and shall not arbitrarily expand the scope of commodities that are not eligible for unconditional return.
The business operator shall mark, in a conspicuous manner, the commodities that are not eligible for unconditional return, and prompt the consumer to confirm at the time of purchase; it shall not make non-applicability of unconditional return a default option for the consumer. Without the consumer's confirmation, the operator shall not refuse unconditional return.
The commodity returned by the consumer shall be intact. If the consumer opens the commodity packaging for inspection purposes, or performs reasonable testing to confirm the quality and function of the commodity without affecting its original quality, function, and appearance, the operator shall accept the return.
The consumer's unconditional return shall follow the principle of good faith, and shall not use the unconditional return rules to harm the legitimate rights and interests of the operator and other consumers.

Article 20 Where a business operator collects a deposit when providing commodities or services, it shall agree in advance with the consumer on the method, procedure, and time limit for refunding the deposit, and shall not impose unreasonable conditions on the refund of the deposit.
If the consumer requests the refund of the deposit and meets the conditions for the refund, the operator shall refund it in a timely manner.

Article 21 Where a business operator decides to cease business or relocate its service premises, it shall, 30 days in advance, announce the operator's valid contact information and other information in a conspicuous position at its business premises, website, online store homepage, etc.

Article 22 Where a business operator provides commodities or services by collecting prepayments, it shall conclude a written contract with the consumer, specifying matters such as the specific content, price or fees of the commodities or services, the method of refunding prepayments, and liability for breach of contract.
After collecting the prepayment, the operator shall provide the commodities or services in accordance with the agreement with the consumer, and shall not degrade the quality of the commodities or services, nor arbitrarily increase the price. If the operator fails to provide the commodities or services as agreed, it shall perform the agreement or refund the prepayment at the request of the consumer.
Where a major business risk arises that may affect the operator's ability to normally provide commodities or services in accordance with the contract or trading practices, the operator shall stop collecting prepayments. Where the operator decides to cease business or relocate its service premises, it shall inform the consumer in advance and perform the obligations specified in Article 21 of these Regulations. The consumer shall have the right, in accordance with relevant national provisions or the contract, to require the operator to continue to perform the obligation of providing commodities or services, or to request a refund of the remaining unused prepayment.

Article 23 A business operator shall protect consumers' personal information according to law. When providing commodities or services, the operator shall not excessively collect consumers' personal information, and shall not compel or constructively compel consumers to consent to the collection and use of personal information unrelated to the business activities by means such as one-time blanket authorization or default authorization.
Where a business operator processes sensitive personal information, including information such as consumers' biometric identification, religious belief, specific identity, medical health, financial accounts, whereabouts, as well as personal information of minors under the age of 14, it shall comply with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 24 Without the consumer's consent, a business operator shall not send commercial information or make commercial phone calls to the consumer. Where the consumer consents to receive commercial information or commercial phone calls, the operator shall provide a clear and convenient method for cancellation. If the consumer chooses to cancel, the operator shall immediately cease sending commercial information or making commercial phone calls.

Article 25 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen guidance on the protection of consumers' rights and interests, organize, coordinate, and supervise relevant administrative departments to fulfill their responsibilities for the protection of consumers' rights and interests, and enhance the level of rule of law in the work of protecting consumers' rights and interests.

Article 26 Where a consumer has a dispute with a business operator over consumer rights and interests, the consumer may file a complaint with the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative departments.
A natural person, legal person, or other organization may report to the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative departments, providing clues that a business operator is suspected of violating the law.

Article 27 The market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative departments shall keep consumer complaint and reporting channels open and standardized, improve the complaint and reporting handling procedures, accept and handle complaints and reports in a timely manner according to law, strengthen the analysis and application of complaint and reporting information, and issue consumer warnings and risk alerts.
Complaints and reports shall comply with laws, regulations, and relevant provisions, and shall not be used to seek improper benefits, infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of business operators, or disrupt the order of the market economy.

Article 28 The market supervision and administration department and other relevant administrative departments shall strengthen coordination and information sharing in the work of protecting consumers' rights and interests, and within their respective functions and duties, implement regulatory measures such as random inspections and testing on the commodities and services provided by business operators, and promptly investigate and punish acts that infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of consumers.

Article 29 The market supervision and administration department and other relevant administrative departments shall strengthen the construction of a credit system in the consumer field, publicly disclose information such as relevant administrative licenses, administrative penalties, random inspection and testing results, and consumer complaints according to law, and impose sanctions on dishonest business operators that violate the law according to law.

Article 30 Relevant administrative departments shall strengthen the promotion and popularization of consumer knowledge, advocate civilized, healthy, and green consumption, and enhance consumers' awareness and ability to protect their rights according to law and rationally; and strengthen legal publicity, administrative guidance, and compliance guidance for business operators to enhance their awareness of operating according to law.

Article 31 The State shall improve the standards, certification, and information disclosure system for green consumption, encourage business operators to disclose information or make commitments on green consumption in respect of commodities and services, and investigate and punish acts of false information disclosure and false commitments according to law.

Article 32 Industry associations, chambers of commerce, and other organizations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, guide and urge business operators to operate lawfully and in good faith, and the industry rules, self-discipline rules, model contracts, and relevant standards formulated by them shall be conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of consumers.

Article 33 The State encourages and supports all organizations and individuals to exercise social supervision over acts that harm the legitimate rights and interests of consumers.
The mass media shall report on matters relating to consumers' rights and interests in a truthful, objective, and fair manner, strengthen the promotion and popularization of knowledge related to consumer rights protection, and exercise public opinion supervision over acts that harm the legitimate rights and interests of consumers.

Article 34 Consumer associations and other consumer organizations established according to law shall perform their duties in accordance with the provisions of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests.

Article 35 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the organizational development of consumer associations and provide necessary financial and other support for consumer associations to perform their duties.

Article 36 Relevant administrative departments shall seriously listen to the opinions and suggestions of consumer associations. For issues of infringement of consumers' legitimate rights and interests reported by consumer associations to relevant administrative departments, the relevant administrative departments shall promptly investigate, handle, and reply; for cases that are placed on file for investigation and punishment, the relevant administrative departments shall inform the consumer associations of the handling results.

Article 37 Consumer associations shall strengthen legal publicity on consumption and consumer guidance, provide consumers with services and support for consumer rights protection, and enhance consumers' ability to safeguard their own legitimate rights and interests.
Consumer associations shall promptly summarize and promote typical cases and experience in protecting consumers' legitimate rights and interests, and guide and support business operators in carrying out business activities in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 38 Consumer associations may organize and carry out activities such as comparative testing, consumer surveys, consumer evaluations, public disclosure of complaint information, submission of complained commodities for expert evaluation, and issuance of consumer tips and warnings, reflecting the status of commodities and services, consumer opinions, and the situation of consumer rights protection.

Article 39 Consumer associations may propose improvement suggestions or conduct guidance talks with relevant business operators and industry organizations on matters of consumer rights protection, strengthen the organization and coordination among consumers, business operators, industry organizations, professional institutions, relevant administrative departments, and other relevant parties, and promote the resolution of important issues concerning the protection of consumers' legitimate rights and interests.

Article 40 Consumer associations may conduct investigations into acts complained of by consumers that harm consumers' legitimate rights and interests, verify the situation with the relevant business operator, and invite the relevant business operator to attend to state facts and opinions, provide evidence, etc.

Article 41 For acts that harm the legitimate rights and interests of many consumers, the China Consumers' Association and the consumer associations established in provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may institute legal proceedings with the People's Court.

Article 42 Consumers shall consume in a civilized and rational manner, enhance their self-protection awareness, safeguard their own legitimate rights and interests according to law, and protect their rights according to law when a consumer dispute arises.

Article 43 The market supervision and administration departments and other relevant administrative departments of people's governments at all levels shall promote and improve a diversified mechanism for resolving consumer disputes, and guide consumers to safeguard their legitimate rights and interests according to law through negotiation, mediation, complaint, arbitration, litigation, and other means.

Article 44 A business operator shall establish a convenient and efficient complaint handling mechanism to resolve consumer disputes in a timely manner.
Business operators shall be encouraged and guided to establish and improve systems such as first-inquiry responsibility, advance compensation, and online dispute resolution, to prevent and resolve consumer disputes in a timely manner.

Article 45 Where a consumer and a business operator have a consumer dispute and request mediation by a consumer association or another mediation organization established according to law, the relevant organization shall handle the matter in a timely manner.

Article 46 Where a consumer and a business operator file a complaint with the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative departments concerning a consumer dispute, they shall provide true identity information, have a clear respondent, specific complaint requests, and factual basis.
The relevant administrative department shall, within 7 working days from the date of receiving the complaint, handle it and inform the consumer. If a decision is made not to accept a complaint that does not comply with the provisions, the department shall inform the consumer of the reasons for not accepting it and other avenues for dispute resolution.
After the relevant administrative department accepts the complaint, if the consumer and the business operator agree to mediation, the relevant administrative department shall promptly mediate according to its duties and complete the mediation within 60 days from the date of acceptance; if mediation fails, it shall terminate the mediation. If expert evaluation or testing is needed during the mediation process, the time for expert evaluation or testing shall not be counted in the 60-day period.
With the consent of the consumer and the business operator, the relevant administrative department may, according to law, entrust the complaint to a consumer association or another mediation organization established according to law for mediation.

Article 47 Where expert evaluation or testing of the quality of commodities or services is required due to a consumer dispute, the consumer and the business operator may negotiate to determine the expert evaluation or testing institution. If they fail to reach a consensus, the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative department that accepted the consumer's complaint may designate an expert evaluation or testing institution.
For major, complex consumer disputes involving the legitimate rights and interests of many consumers, the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative department may include them in the random inspection and testing procedures and entrust an institution with corresponding qualifications to conduct expert evaluation or testing.

Article 48 Where a business operator provides commodities or services in violation of the relevant provisions of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests and these Regulations, and infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of consumers, it shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 49 Where a business operator engages in fraudulent conduct in providing commodities or services, the consumer shall have the right to demand compensation from the operator in accordance with Article 55, paragraph 1 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests. However, this does not apply if there are defects in the labels, instructions, promotional materials, etc., of the commodities or services that do not affect the quality of the commodities or services and will not mislead consumers.
If a person obtains compensation from a business operator by fraudulent means such as inserting items, switching goods, forging, tampering with production dates, or fabricating facts, or extorts the operator, the provisions of Article 55, paragraph 1 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests shall not apply, and the matter shall be handled in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on Public Security Administration Punishments and other relevant laws and regulations; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 50 Where a business operator violates the provisions of Articles 10 to 14, 16, 17, and 19 to 21 of these Regulations, if other relevant laws and regulations have provisions on the penalty authority and penalty methods, those provisions shall be followed; if laws and regulations have no such provisions, the market supervision and administration department or other relevant administrative department shall order rectification, and may, depending on the circumstances, impose a single or concurrent warning, confiscation of illegal gains, or a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains, or, if there are no illegal gains, a fine of not more than 300,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, order suspension of business for rectification and revoke the business license.
Where a business operator violates the provisions of Article 22 of these Regulations, the relevant administrative department shall order rectification, and may, depending on the circumstances, impose a single or concurrent warning, confiscation of illegal gains, or a fine of not less than one time but not more than ten times the illegal gains, or, if there are no illegal gains, a fine of not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, order suspension of business for rectification and revoke the business license.
Where a business operator violates other provisions of these Regulations, the operator shall be punished in accordance with Article 56 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests.

Article 51 Where a business operator voluntarily eliminates or mitigates the harmful consequences of an illegal act, or the illegal act is minor and corrected in a timely manner without causing harmful consequences, or it is a first-time illegal act with minor harmful consequences that is corrected in a timely manner, the operator shall be given a lighter or mitigated administrative penalty, or no penalty, in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 52 Where staff members of relevant administrative departments fail to perform their duties of protecting consumers' rights and interests in accordance with these Regulations, or neglect their duties or cover up acts of business operators that infringe upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests, they shall be given sanctions according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 53 These Regulations shall come into force as of July 1, 2024.
